observations.seen: The ball casts a soft blob shadow and the gates cast colored shadow shapes on the track. The contact shadows look washed out, though, and the gate shadows are pale tinted rectangles rather than grounded occlusion.

The red ball has a strong white specular highlight and a rim reflection, and the gates reflect faintly in the glossy track. The reflections are stylized and generic, with no sense of the pink sky being reflected.

The ball sits low and centered at roughly 8–12% of the frame, smaller than the 18–25% target. In frame 4 the bottom of the screen is dominated by a large red paint splat that pulls the eye away from the subject.

The camera is a behind-the-ball chase cam, not the side-on follow the recipe expects. It is wide-angle, more than 50°, so the edge rail spheres are strongly stretched. Speed lines in the sky read well.

There is a warm bloom haze near the horizon and radial speed streaks. The overall image looks hazy and pastel, which lowers contrast. There is no visible tonemapping punch or color grading toward daylight-outdoor.
The paint splatter particles and gate drips suggest motion and impact feedback. From stills alone, the trailing splat decal looks oversized and blobby.
Sunset backlight with warm horizon glow and pink sky. It reads as golden hour rather than a 3/4 front daylight key.
Floating grassy islands, towers, hot-air balloons, rock spires and a cloud sea. The world is cohesive and charming, but its palette is pinks and purples rather than greens and sky blue.
Distance fades into pink haze and the clouds are layered. The fog is heavier than the 0.0025 target and flattens the midground.
Glossy candy gates with drips, a wood-plank track, and a glassy ball. Materials are consistent and stylized.
Gates with drip geometry, a gold star coin, a shield pickup and island props are clean, low-poly stylized assets.
Hearts, a power meter, a score panel, a combo counter and a power-up timer, all in clean rounded styling. The title card includes accessibility toggles.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
